method: tools/parity/oidc-differential.cjs against isolated copies of the API-initialized pinned v2.37.2 fixture, one ephemeral local RS256 provider; 20 Node-versus-Go cases with raw redirect Location comparison, including the empty-code_verifier no-session edge including web OIDC, real-socket user_added, mobile PKCE redirect, token exchange, persisted user/session state, and replay behavior
normalization: JWT signatures and random token bytes are not retained; algorithms and claims are compared, normalizing only UUID-valued identifiers and timestamps. Each ID-token nonce is checked against the nonce from that same side authorization flow.
Node and Go use separate copied fixture directories and database files. Only fixture-specific backup paths are normalized in API settings; persisted user fields and session counts remain compared.

JSON object member order is canonicalized for Socket.IO payload comparison because JSON object order is not semantically significant; array order, scalar values, null versus empty, and linked-user raw persisted extraData text remain strict.
limits: Compared web auto-registration, provider error, state replay, expired ID token, email linking, auto-registration denial, invalid nonce/issuer/audience/signature, selected admin-only user_added event, mobile redirect/PKCE validation, mobile app redirect and state consumption/replay, valid mobile token exchange and consumed callback-session replay.

Selected web/mobile start and successful callback cookies compare name, stable value, Max-Age, Path, Expires, HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite and signed connect.sid; claims and selected persisted user/session effects are compared. Mobile invalid-verifier/provider errors, in-memory state expiry, failure/logout cookie clearing, other callback variants and general Socket.IO inventory remain unverified.
Only fixture-specific backup paths, UUID identifiers and timestamps are normalized. Null/empty distinctions, response shapes, arrays and raw persisted extraData remain strict.
